video_meta.title: The Marshmallow Test Lie That Fooled Everyone
video_meta.description:
For decades, the famous marshmallow test taught us that childhood self-control dictates lifelong success. But a massive modern replication has turned this comforting psychological dogma entirely on its head. 🍬

In this video:
🧠 🍯 The famous Stanford marshmallow room experiment
👶 ⏳ How resisting a sweet treat supposedly meant future wealth
📉 🔍 The surprising large-scale modern replication study
💰 🏫 Discovering the hidden role of family wealth and trust
🧐 ⚖️ Re-evaluating willpower versus socioeconomic reality

📚 SOURCES & IMPORTANT NOTE
Tyler, C. R., et al. (2018). "Replicating and Extending Mischel and EBB's Experimental Paradigms." Psychological Science, 29(11), 1837-1847. IMPORTANT: The original 1960s findings by Walter Mischel have been significantly challenged, showing that socioeconomic background and environmental trust play a far larger role in delayed gratification than innate willpower.

So what do you think — is willpower just a myth masking privilege, or does self-control still matter?

00:00 The Tempting Marshmallow
00:35 The Stanford Experiment
01:10 The Promise of Success
01:45 The Modern Re-examination
02:25 Rethinking Willpower

#Psychology #MarshmallowTest #BehavioralScience #SelfControl #CognitiveScience
